prompt:
Warm editorial ink-and-wash illustration on a warm cream ground: a loose confident ink line with soft transparent washes over it, muted earth palette of cream, rust, ochre, mustard, sage and warm grey, quiet and hand-made, the register of a good picture book rather than a comic. Character reference: TOMAS, a boy of about SEVEN. CROPPED DARK HAIR and a ROUND, soft face. A tee shirt with HORIZONTAL RUST-AND-CREAM STRIPES, and plain shorts. ONE SOCK IS SLUMPED DOWN AROUND HIS ANKLE and the other is pulled up. He stands in a relaxed neutral pose, FULL BODY visible head to feet, front three-quarter view, arms loose at his sides. He is a small serious child, calm and watchful, NOT mugging, NOT pulling a funny face, NOT waving, NOT a cartoon scamp. Plain empty cream background with no scenery and no props. Render ONE single image only. This is NOT a contact sheet, NOT a grid, NOT a multi-panel study sheet, NOT a turnaround strip. No panel borders, no captions, no labels, no annotation text of any kind. ABSOLUTELY NOT, these are the rejected poles of this style and any of them is a failure: neon, 3D or CGI or Pixar rendering, glossy plastic, HUD or arc-reactor comic vocabulary, neo-comic styling, photorealism, airbrushing, lens flare, heavy drop shadows.

READABLE SURFACES FACE THEIR READER: any book, page, letter, scroll or sign a character is reading or writing faces THAT CHARACTER, never the camera. Compose over-the-shoulder or from behind so the surface genuinely faces them. Any handwriting is abstract handwriting-like line work with NO real readable letters.

NO USER INTERFACE ANYWHERE: no windows, menu bars, buttons, icons, toolbars, panels, form fields, cursors, floating rectangles or screenshot-like elements. Screens carry only soft glow or vague painterly shapes.
